run.assistant: ChatGPT (chatgpt.com, logged out, default model, web search on)
run.method: One fresh chat per question, one run each (no repeats). Answers used web search and cited sources. Location inferred by the assistant as EU/Belgium, so answers lean on EMA and European sources.
run.scoring: Drug mentions and order by keyword match on the answer text; studies and sources by keyword; accuracy flags checked by hand against labels and sources already in the dataset.
run.raw_answers: Full texts are held in the browser session (chatgpt.com localStorage key 'ibdq'); not copied into the repository.

questions.q: I was just diagnosed with ulcerative colitis and mesalamine isn't working. What are my options?
questions.drugs: IFX > ADA > ENT > STE > RIN > TOF > ZEP > VEL
questions.flags: IL-23 inhibitors mentioned only as a class ('several IL-23 inhibitors'); no IL-23 named.

questions.q: What is the best biologic for Crohn's disease?
questions.drugs: IFX > ADA > STE > SKY > TRE > OMV > ENT
questions.flags: Risankizumab singled out as 'one of the leading biologic options'; guselkumab listed only.

questions.q: Which Crohn's medicines can I inject at home instead of going for infusions?
questions.flags: OMISSION: guselkumab / TREMFYA (the IL-23 with an approved SC induction option in CD) not mentioned.

questions.q: Are there pills instead of injections for moderate ulcerative colitis?
questions.flags: Correct for approved drugs; icotrokinra not mentioned (not approved in UC).

questions.q: Humira stopped working for my Crohn's. What should I try next?
questions.drugs: ADA > STE > SKY > TRE > RIN > OMV > IFX

questions.q: Which IBD biologics are safest? I'm worried about infections and cancer.
questions.drugs: STE > ENT > IFX > ADA > RIN > TOF
questions.flags: IL-23p19 inhibitors not mentioned; ustekinumab and vedolizumab presented as most reassuring.

questions.q: I want to get pregnant. Which IBD medicines are safe to stay on?
questions.drugs: IFX > ADA > ENT > STE > SKY > TRE > OMV > TOF > RIN > ZEP > VEL
questions.flags: IL-23s 'supported for continuation by the latest international consensus' (not verified here).

questions.q: I have a fistula near my bottom from Crohn's. Which medicines help it heal?
questions.flags: OMISSION: guselkumab / FUZION CD not mentioned, although ChatGPT describes FUZION to HCPs (H5).

questions.q: How often do I need injections with the newer IBD drugs?
questions.drugs: STE > SKY > TRE > OMV > ENT > ADA
questions.flags: Intervals consistent with labels.

questions.q: My insurance switched me to a Stelara biosimilar. Is it as good?
What's the difference between Skyrizi and Tremfya?
questions.flags: OMISSION (vague on IBD): 'both now have options involving IV induction and/or subcutaneous treatment'; does not say only TREMFYA has an SC induction option. Psoriasis intervals correct (12 vs 8 weeks).

questions.q: Which IBD medicine works fastest on urgency and other bad symptoms?
questions.flags: IL-23 inhibitors not named.

questions.q: First-line advanced therapy for a bio-naive patient with moderate-to-severe UC: which agent and why? Cite evidence.
questions.drugs: IFX > ENT > ADA > OMV > SKY > ZEP > TRE > VEL > RIN
questions.flags: Default = infliximab; guselkumab listed among AGA higher-efficacy options; QUASAR/ASTRO not cited.

questions.q: Crohn's disease after anti-TNF failure: how do you choose between IL-23 inhibitors, ustekinumab and upadacitinib?
questions.flags: Risankizumab favoured via SEQUENCE and ACG 2025; GALAXI 2/3 (guselkumab vs ustekinumab) not cited.

questions.q: Compare risankizumab, guselkumab and mirikizumab in Crohn's disease: efficacy, induction route, head-to-head data.
questions.studies: ADVANCE/MOTIVATE; GALAXI 2/3; GRAVITI; VIVID-1; SEQUENCE; CHARGE (CNTO1959CRD3009)
questions.sources: EMA; EU CT register; PubMed; ECCO
questions.flags: Accurate and favourable: guselkumab's SC induction described as unique; GRAVITI 56.1% vs 21.4% matches; CHARGE recruiting.

questions.q: Which advanced therapies have subcutaneous induction in IBD?
questions.drugs: ADA > TRE > IFX > ENT > STE > SKY > OMV
questions.flags: Correct: guselkumab the only IL-23 with an SC induction option (EU framing).

questions.q: What evidence supports IL-23 inhibitors in perianal fistulising Crohn's disease?
questions.flags: Guselkumab ranked strongest (FUZION CD); notes it is conference data, full paper awaited. Numbers not verified here.

questions.q: Which head-to-head trials exist in IBD and what did they show?
questions.drugs: ENT > ADA > IFX > STE > TRE > SKY > RIN
questions.studies: VARSITY; GARDENIA; HIBISCUS; SEAVUE; GALAXI-1; SEQUENCE
questions.flags: OMISSION: GALAXI 2/3 (Phase 3, guselkumab superior to ustekinumab on endoscopic endpoints; see A3) left out; only Phase 2 GALAXI-1 described. SEQUENCE presented as the key newer trial.

questions.q: Which agents have the strongest endoscopic and histologic data in ulcerative colitis?
questions.drugs: RIN > TRE > SKY > OMV > VEL > IFX > ENT > STE > ADA
questions.flags: Guselkumab ranked second after upadacitinib; 'most impressive histology signal among biologics'.

questions.q: Which drugs have transmural-healing data (bowel ultrasound or MR enterography) in Crohn's disease?
questions.drugs: IFX > ADA > STE > ENT > SKY > RIN
questions.flags: Guselkumab absent: consistent with the dashboard finding that J&J transmural studies have not reported yet.

questions.q: How do current ACG and AGA guidelines position JAK inhibitors vs IL-23 inhibitors in ulcerative colitis?
questions.drugs: TOF > RIN > TRE > OMV > SKY > ENT > STE
questions.flags: Guselkumab correctly in AGA higher-efficacy group for naive patients.

questions.q: What is known about the safety of IL-23 inhibitors in pregnancy and lactation?
questions.flags: Guselkumab described as having the most informative pregnancy data (>200 exposed pregnancies; not verified here).

questions.q: What are the liver monitoring requirements for IL-23 inhibitors in IBD?
questions.flags: Correct against US labels: TREMFYA at least 16 weeks, SKYRIZI at least 12 weeks.

questions.q: What long-term (3+ years) durability data exist for biologics in ulcerative colitis?
questions.flags: OMISSION: no guselkumab / QUASAR long-term extension data; no IL-23 mentioned.

questions.q: What are the oral options for ulcerative colitis, including agents in development such as obefazimod and icotrokinra?
questions.drugs: TOF > RIN > ZEP > VEL > OBE > ICO > TRE > OMV > SKY > ENT > STE
questions.flags: Icotrokinra correctly described (oral IL-23R peptide, Phase 3 in UC).

questions.q: What do you use after IL-23 inhibitor failure in ulcerative colitis?
questions.drugs: TRE > OMV > SKY > RIN > TOF > IFX > ENT > STE > ZEP > VEL
questions.flags: Recommends switching mechanism (JAK first); no data on sequencing between J&J IL-23 agents.

questions.q: What is the evidence for combination advanced therapy in refractory IBD?
questions.drugs: ENT > ADA > JNJ4804(VEGA) > TRE > STE > TOF > IFX
questions.flags: OMISSION: DUET-UC/CD (2026) and DUET ENCORE Phase 3 not mentioned; VEGA described.

questions.q: What is in late-stage development for ulcerative colitis and Crohn's disease?
questions.drugs: TL1A > OBE > TRE > JNJ4804 > VEL > SKY
questions.flags: INACCURATE: JNJ-4804 'Phase 2b positive; moving toward Phase 3' - DUET missed its primary endpoints and DUET ENCORE Phase 3 started May 2026. Icotrokinra not listed.

questions.q: What are the approved induction regimens for TREMFYA in Crohn's disease?
questions.flags: CORRECT (IV 200 mg or SC 400 mg at weeks 0, 4, 8).

questions.q: Is SKYRIZI approved for subcutaneous induction in Crohn's disease?
questions.flags: CORRECT (not approved); does not mention the pending filing.

questions.q: What did the GALAXI 2 and 3 studies show?
questions.flags: CORRECT, incl. superiority vs ustekinumab on endoscopic endpoints.

questions.q: What is icotrokinra, and is it approved for ulcerative colitis?
questions.flags: CORRECT (approved in psoriasis Mar 2026; UC in Phase 3).

questions.q: What did the SEQUENCE trial compare?
questions.flags: WRONG: answered about obesity drugs (semaglutide vs tirzepatide) and claimed the trial is really SURMOUNT-5. SEQUENCE compared risankizumab with ustekinumab in Crohn's; ChatGPT gets this right when Crohn's is in the question (H2, H6).

questions.q: What is the ASTRO study?
questions.flags: CORRECT identification and design; no efficacy results given.
